subject.title: Feishu auto-reply and `message` tool path bypass `message_sending` / `reply_payload_sending` / `message_sent` plugin hooks

question: Should normal channel inbound messages run global `inbound_claim`, or should `inbound_claim` remain limited to plugin-owned bindings while passive observers use `message_received` or a new narrower observer hook?
rationale: Outbound hook parity is a clear bug, but changing `inbound_claim` coverage affects plugin first-claim-wins semantics and could alter which plugin owns or observes inbound channel traffic.

options.title: Fix outbound parity and defer inbound claim
options.body: Repair Feishu prebuilt auto-replies so outbound hooks fire, then track the passive-observer inbound API as a separate design decision.

options.title: Expand inbound_claim globally
options.body: Run `inbound_claim` on normal channel inbound traffic too, with explicit ordering and security tests for first-claim-wins behavior.

options.title: Add a narrower observer hook
options.body: Keep `inbound_claim` ownership-scoped and add or document a passive observer seam for Feishu bot-to-bot detection.

recommendation.title: Fix outbound parity and defer inbound claim
recommendation.body: Repair Feishu prebuilt auto-replies so outbound hooks fire, then track the passive-observer inbound API as a separate design decision.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision is mainly about plugin API and channel hook semantics, where the history points to plugin/channel seam ownership.
